rules.reason: CTA barrier participant counts must satisfy the documented domain.
Aligned CTA barriers require converged participation.
Active CTA barrier invocations cannot be incompatibly reused before reset.
Completed CTA barriers establish the documented order and visibility.
mbarrier operations require a live initialized object.
mbarrier storage, layout, alignment, and count values must remain in range.
Initialization creates a fresh lifecycle and defined phase state.
Arrival updates the pending-arrival ledger without violating its domain.
Arrive-drop updates current and subsequent phase arrival counts.
Expected and completed transaction bytes share one bounded signed ledger.
A phase completes only when arrival and transaction ledgers both reach zero.
At least one successful wait must observe a completed phase before the next phase receives its first arrive-on.
Wait state and parity must resolve to the current or immediately previous supported generation.
Only a successful wait provides the specified acquire and visibility effect.
A cp.async issue opens source-read and destination-write windows until completion.
Classic cp.async groups are formed per issuing thread, including legal empty groups.
Writes within one cp.async group are unordered and overlapping destinations are invalid.
wait_group N closes all but the newest N group windows and provides only its documented visibility.
TMA and bulk issues create async-proxy source and destination access windows.
Bulk transfer size, alignment, range, and descriptor constraints must be established.
Each logical issue contributes its copied byte count once to the tracked mbarrier generation.
Generic consumers require successful observation of the corresponding TMA barrier phase.
Read-only and full bulk-group waits close different source and destination endpoints.
Generic/async handoff requires matching fence direction, scope, state space, and region.
WGMMA requires sm_90a and an exact warpgroup participant identity.
WGMMA protocol operations require warpgroup convergence.
Register operands and accumulators require the documented WGMMA fence ordering.
A register fence does not replace the shared-memory generic-to-async proxy fence.
WGMMA groups are monotonic per warpgroup and may be empty.
wait_group N establishes the result-ready frontier for older WGMMA groups.
Accumulator or register-A access before the covering result wait is invalid.
Shared operands remain asynchronously readable until their group is covered by a legal wait.
Overlapping operations conflict when at least one is a write.
A conflicting pair is a data race when neither causality nor moral strength orders it.
Cross-proxy causality is preserved only by a fence covering the relevant direction, scope, state space, and alias.
Conflicts must be checked against complete asynchronous access windows rather than issue points.
